title: Chapter 135 — Internal Communication
intro: Great customer service starts behind the counter.

sections.title: The Sales-to-Delivery Handoff
sections.content:
The most dropped ball in appliance retail. The salesperson promised white-glove install with waterline hookup. The delivery ticket says 'drop at door.' The customer is furious and the delivery crew has no idea what was sold.

Every promise made during the sale must be documented on the delivery ticket. Installation type, haul-away, accessories included, special instructions, customer expectations. If it is not on the ticket, it does not happen.

sections.title: Leaving Notes That Help
sections.content:
CRM notes should help the next person, not just check a box. Bad note: 'Spoke to customer.' Good note: 'Customer choosing between Bosch 500 and 800 series dishwashers. Main concern is drying performance. Husband prefers 500 for budget, wife wants 800 for CrystalDry. Follow up Thursday after they discuss.'

The second note lets any rep pick up the conversation seamlessly. The first note is useless.

sections.title: Never Throw Coworkers Under the Bus
sections.content:
The customer does not need to know about internal disagreements, scheduling conflicts, or who made the mistake. They need to know it is being fixed.

'I am sorry about the confusion — let me sort this out for you right now.' Not: 'Yeah, the delivery team messed that up.' Own the resolution on behalf of the team, regardless of whose fault it was.
